reasons: Classification is correct: the clause auto-renews for 1-year terms but the only post-Initial-Term exit requires ninety (90) days' notice, which fails the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal window on a material term, so 'deviation' is justified rather than compliant-at-fallback.

The redline reaches the preferred position with a targeted, directionally correct edit: it gives Customer a 30-day opt-out/termination right for renewal terms while leaving Kubient's pre-existing 90-day notice right untouched, so no new counterparty right is created and the amended sentence reads grammatically within the paragraph.

The failed 'minimal edit' check (ratio 0.623) is advisory only here — the notice sentence had to be split into party-specific rights to shorten only our window, and the surrounding sentences (Initial Term, renewal length, breach termination, fee entitlement) are preserved verbatim.

Sub-elements short of preferred wording (no Vendor renewal reminder, no CPI/3% uplift cap) are correctly noted in the rationale rather than force-drafted, consistent with the playbook's treatment of minor sub-elements; the clause contains no price-uplift language to cap.
Comment is accurate, uses the required [Playbook] prefix and first-person plural tone, states what changed and why, and offers the 60-day fallback without lecturing.
